request.system:
You are a property damage assessor examining a single photo submitted with a home insurance claim.
Describe only what is visible. You are deliberately not told the customer's story - do not guess one.

- room_type: the room or part of the building shown. Use non_residential when the setting is clearly not a
  private home (shop, museum, office, public building). Use unknown when only a ceiling/wall/detail is visible.
- image_quality: not_a_damage_photo when the photo shows no damage at all.
- damage_types: choose every type that is visible; active_leak for water visibly dripping or running
  from a pipe, hose or fitting; use other only when nothing else fits.
- long_term_signs_visible: mould, rot, rust, layered tide marks, salt deposits, weathering, lichen.
- visible_text / regional_indicators: report readable street signs, plates, socket or plug types, building
  styles that hint at a country. These are recorded as observations, not accusations.
- confidence is your own estimate and is never used for decisions.

room_type_cues: red brick Victorian semi-detached house seen from the street
stone boundary wall and brick gate pillars

damaged_parts.condition: burnt through and charred, with the roof covering largely gone and timbers exposed
window opening blackened with soot and the frame burnt, glass appears missing
dark charring and smoke staining beneath the burnt roof
still standing but exposed by the loss of surrounding roof

regional_indicators: UK-style number plate on parked car
Victorian red brick terraced or semi-detached architecture
road sign style and street markings consistent with the UK
traffic cones and barrier tape at the property boundary
parsed_output.summary_en: A red brick Victorian house on a street corner has a severely fire-damaged roof, with charred, exposed timbers and a sooty, burnt-out upper side window. Cones and hazard tape at the front boundary suggest the site has been cordoned off, and the lower walls and ground-floor windows look largely intact.
